descriptors.concept_name: Audit Procedures When Non-Compliance Is Identified Or Suspected
descriptors.definition: When an auditor encounters indications of potential non-compliance with legal requirements, they must gather facts regarding the act and its environment to assess financial statement impacts. If management fails to substantiate compliance, the auditor must consider legal consultation and evaluate the effect on audit evidence reliability and overall risk assessment.
inclusion: Gathering facts about suspected legal breaches
Consulting management and those charged with governance
Evaluating audit opinion implications for unverified compliance
exclusion: Definitive legal adjudication of illegal acts
Unilateral reporting to external enforcement without governance escalation
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general risk assessment by focusing specifically on verified or suspected regulatory infractions rather than broad operational errors.

descriptors.concept_name: Reporting of Identified or Suspected Non-Compliance
descriptors.definition: The auditor communicates identified non-compliance matters to those charged with governance unless inconsequential or involving management complicity, in which case escalation to higher authorities or legal counsel is necessary. Uncorrected material non-compliance results in modified audit opinions regarding the financial statements.
inclusion: Escalating material infractions to governance or higher supervisory bodies
Modifying the audit report for uncorrected material non-compliance
Issuing scope limitations when evidence is blocked by management
exclusion: Direct external reporting absent specific statutory mandates
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial fact-finding procedures by focusing strictly on formal communication channels and audit report modifications.

descriptors.definition: The auditor must formally record all identified or suspected instances of legal non-compliance along with the substance of discussions held with management, governance representatives, and external parties. This documentation preserves the audit trail regarding how potential statutory violations were evaluated.
inclusion: Recording details of legal non-compliance findings
Documenting outcomes of consultations with governance
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from the substantive audit procedures or reporting steps because it solely targets the permanent recording of findings and discussions.

descriptors.concept_name: Definition and Governance Structure of Those Charged with Governance
descriptors.definition: Those charged with governance comprise individuals or organizations entrusted with overseeing an entity's strategic direction, operational accountability, and financial reporting obligations. Governance structures vary significantly by entity size and legal framework, ranging from separate supervisory boards to sole owner-managers.
inclusion: Board of directors
Supervisory boards
Proprietors, partners, or trustees
exclusion: Operational management personnel acting exclusively in an executive capacity without governance oversight duties (unless overlapping in smaller entities)
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes those overseeing strategic accountability from operational managers, though both roles may overlap in smaller enterprises.

descriptors.concept_name: Objectives of Auditor in Accordance with SA 260
descriptors.definition: The auditor must clearly communicate statutory audit responsibilities and scope while fostering effective two-way dialogue with governance bodies. This process ensures auditors obtain relevant audit information and provide timely, significant observations regarding the financial reporting process.
inclusion: Communicating auditor responsibilities and engagement scope
Obtaining relevant information from governance
Promoting continuous dialogue
exclusion: Relieving management of financial statement preparation duties
nearby_distinctions: Focused on establishing communication objectives rather than executing substantive testing procedures.

descriptors.definition: Auditors must communicate their core responsibilities regarding financial statement audits alongside the planned scope and timing of the engagement. This dialogue helps those charged with governance understand audit consequences, discuss risk and materiality concepts, and provide supplementary insights.
inclusion: Communicating the division of audit responsibilities
Discussing planned audit scope and timing parameters
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from independence disclosures because it specifically addresses engagement parameters and auditor duties.

descriptors.concept_name: Communication of Auditor’s Independence in Case of Listed Entities
descriptors.definition: For listed entities, auditors must formally communicate compliance with ethical independence requirements, detailing all relationships and fees for audit and non-audit services. Additionally, the auditor must disclose any applied safeguards used to mitigate identified threats to independence.
inclusion: Fee disclosures for audit and non-audit services
Statements of compliance with ethical independence norms
Descriptions of safeguards against independence threats
exclusion: Standard scope and timing disclosures applicable to non-listed entities without independence breakdowns
nearby_distinctions: Mandated specifically for listed entities, requiring rigorous fee breakdowns and safeguard evaluations not strictly required for private entities under the same standard.

descriptors.concept_name: Documentation and Overview of Joint Audits
descriptors.definition: Auditors must document all oral and written communications mandated by governance standards, specifying the timing and recipients of such notices. Furthermore, joint audits involve multiple independent auditors collaborating to examine financial statements and issue a shared audit report.
inclusion: Retaining copies of written governance communications
Logging dates and recipients of oral communications
Collaborative multi-auditor financial statement examination
exclusion: Principal-component auditor relationships governed by separate standards
nearby_distinctions: Bridges governance documentation requirements with the foundational principles of multi-auditor joint engagements.

descriptors.concept_name: Framework and Objectives of Joint Audits
descriptors.definition: Joint audits establish uniform principles and coordinated work methodologies for multiple auditors appointed to evaluate an entity's financial statements. The framework defines distinct coverage zones while delineating individual versus collective professional responsibilities.
inclusion: Establishing unified audit strategies across joint teams
Identifying specific operational areas for each auditor
Clarifying shared accountability lines
exclusion: Relationships between principal auditors and independent component auditors
nearby_distinctions: Differs from single-auditor models by requiring formal synchronization and shared governance among distinct auditing firms.

descriptors.concept_name: Objectives and Work Allocation in Joint Audits
descriptors.definition: Joint auditors must establish a cooperative framework that divides audit areas based on operational units, locations, or financial statement items. Certain high-risk or critical areas are examined collectively by all joint auditors rather than being segregated.
inclusion: Allocating work by business units or financial statement accounts
Designating unpartitioned common areas for joint inspection
Aligning engagement reporting objectives
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on the strategic division of tasks and common review areas rather than general audit planning.

descriptors.concept_name: Audit Planning and Risk Assessment in Joint Audits
descriptors.definition: Engagement partners and core teams from all joint audit firms must collaborate to formulate an overarching audit strategy and joint plan. This planning phase accounts for preliminary engagement findings, resource allocations, and material misstatement risks.
inclusion: Joint formulation of audit strategy and plans
Assessment of material misstatement risks across teams
Resource allocation and historical knowledge integration
exclusion: Independent, uncoordinated planning by individual joint firms
nearby_distinctions: Emphasizes mandatory cross-firm collaboration during the initial risk assessment and planning stages.

descriptors.concept_name: Responsibility and Co-ordination among Joint Auditors
descriptors.definition: Joint auditors remain individually accountable for executing procedures within their allocated segments, but share joint and several liability for undivided work, common audit decisions, and statutory compliance. Auditors must maintain active coordination and communicate inter-area findings in writing before audit completion.
inclusion: Individual liability for assigned units or financial captions
Shared liability for unallocated and common review areas
Written communication of cross-segment findings between auditors
exclusion: Absolute immunity of one joint auditor for errors discovered in another's clearly unshared domain if warning signs were mutually evident
nearby_distinctions: Establishes a precise boundary between segregated individual execution duties and collective responsibilities shared across all joint firms.
